title: Policy Watch Findings 001
purpose: Publish initial evidence boundaries and record-first conclusions from the uploaded video leads and policy-watch lanes.
boundary: These are preliminary findings. They describe what the site can responsibly track now, not final claims about private intent.

findings.grade: A for public-framework existence, C for control interpretation
findings.title: Agenda 2030 is a real public policy framework; interpretation requires source routes
findings.finding: The policy framework exists and can be tracked through public documents, targets, indicators and national/local implementation. Claims about hidden purpose require separate evidence.

findings.grade: B for system trend, C for intent
findings.title: Payment, identity and data systems are the key measurable lanes
findings.finding: The most useful tracker lanes are payment rails, wallet systems, identity systems, public-service logins, data-sharing rules and vendor contracts.

findings.title: Family-name claims require current records
findings.finding: Named family claims from the uploaded video are leads, not conclusions. The site should track current filings, foundations, holdings and board links before making any influence claim.

findings.title: Epstein redaction dispute is a live missing-record issue
findings.finding: The DOJ redaction dispute should be tracked as a disclosure and missing-record problem until the response filing, redaction log and any less-redacted set are reviewed.

nextAction: Feed findings into Matrix Brain, Policy Watch, Trigger Watchtower and future verified record cards.
